instruction: Make all slide titles red and underline them for emphasis.

command: import pyautogui; import time; pyautogui.hotkey('ctrl', 's'); time.sleep(0.5);

metadata.explanation: Task requires formatting all slide titles with red color (255, 0, 0) and underline. The evaluator extracts title formatting from all slides in the presentation and checks that each title has red color and underline enabled. Score is proportional to the number of titles that pass both checks. Verified presentation has 5 slides with titles.
metadata.scoring_breakdown: Proportional score: each correctly formatted title contributes 1/5 to final score

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly checks BOTH requirements: red color (255, 0, 0) AND underline formatting
Getter extracts title formatting from ALL slides, not just one slide
Metric correctly handles expected parameter (directly accesses expected.get('color') and expected.get('underline') since expected IS the rules dict)
Appropriate postconfig saves file with Ctrl+S to ensure changes are persisted before verification
Proportional scoring correctly implemented: passed_titles / total_titles
Color tolerance (20) provides practical fuzzy matching for RGB colors
Expected values are semantically correct: [255, 0, 0] for red, true for underline
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: Getter only checks first run in first paragraph of each title (getters/pptx.py:66-77). If titles have mixed formatting (some words red, others not), only first word is checked. This is acceptable for uniform formatting tasks but may miss partial formatting.
Minor: Metadata claims '5 slides with titles' but this wasn't verified against actual file content. Consider verifying slide count matches actual presentation.
